verdict.rationale: Skyfire claims tokens "conform to the open KYAPay protocol, an industry specification" (skyfire-supp-3), but no versioned spec document is discoverable — the OpenAPI/swagger probe returned 404s across all candidate paths (skyfire-probe-2), and every actual protocol operation (token creation, charging, introspection) requires a Skyfire-issued API key tied to a signed-up agent account (skyfire-docs-1, skyfire-supp-8), with the live introspect endpoint rejecting unauthenticated calls (skyfire-probe-rt-1). This contradicts the 'read and implement without signing anything' requirement even though the vendor markets the token format as open. Missing for 10: a publicly hosted versioned specification file/repo, evidence of third-party implementations built without a Skyfire account, and confirmation that core commerce flows (charge, settle) are actually protocol-level rather than proprietary API calls.
